bib.title: 6 Fine-tuning for classification (chapter of Build a Large Language Model From Scratch)

question: How do you adapt a pretrained GPT-style LLM into a spam / not-spam classifier by replacing the output head and fine-tuning on labelled data?
contributions: Contrasts instruction fine-tuning with classification fine-tuning
Worked example: replace the 50,257-way output layer with a 2-way head, fine-tune last block + final LayerNorm, evaluate accuracy

method.summary: Loads pretrained GPT-2 small, replaces the 50,257-way out_head with a 2-way linear layer, freezes all but the head, last transformer block and final LayerNorm, and fine-tunes with cross-entropy on the last-token logits for 5 epochs.

datasets.name: SMS Spam Collection
datasets.size: 5,572 messages (4,825 ham, 747 spam); balanced to 747 per class
datasets.split: 70% train / 10% validation / 20% test; 130 train, 19 val, 38 test batches of 8
datasets.preprocessing: undersample ham with random_state=123; labels ham=0 spam=1; GPT-2 tiktoken; pad with 50256 to longest training length (120 tokens); shuffle random_state=123

training.steps: inferred: 130 batches x 5 epochs (last logged step 600)
training.hardware: M3 MacBook Air (about 6 min); V100 or A100 under half a minute

inference.decoding: argmax over 2 logits of last token
inference.prompting: none for classifier; baseline prompt 'Is the following text 'spam'? Answer with 'yes' or 'no': ...'

eval.protocol: Full-set accuracy on train/val/test after training; in-training estimates on 5 batches

limits: Single run, single seed (torch.manual_seed(123)); no variance reported.
Accuracy only; no precision/recall/F1 although dataset undersampled to balance.
Per-epoch accuracies in training log use only 5 batches (eval_iter=5), so are noisy.
Layer-choice experiments are deferred to appendix B, not in this chapter.
The pretrained model without instruction tuning cannot follow the spam prompt (Sec 6.4), shown by one example only.
Exercises 6.1-6.3 (longer context, full fine-tune, first token) are left to the reader.
practices: Classification fine-tuning needs less data and compute than instruction fine-tuning but is confined to its trained classes (Sec 6.1).
Balance imbalanced classes by undersampling (here 747 per class) to keep the dataset small (Sec 6.2).
Pad every message with token 50256 to the longest training sequence rather than truncating to the shortest (Sec 6.3).
Replace the output head and fine-tune the head, last transformer block and final LayerNorm; freeze the rest (Sec 6.5).
Use the logits of the last token only, since under the causal mask it sees all prior tokens (Sec 6.5).
Use cross-entropy as a differentiable proxy for non-differentiable accuracy (Sec 6.6).
Five epochs is a reasonable starting point; adjust by watching train/val loss gap (Sec 6.7).
To close a val/test gap, raise dropout or weight decay (Sec 6.7).
